name: Annotating the first mention only, and what it does to a weighted graph
name_fr: N'annoter que la première mention, et ce que ça fait à un graphe pondéré

origin.organisation: van Erp, Mendes, Paulheim, Ilievski, Plu, Rizzo, Waitelonis
origin.campaign: Evaluating Entity Linking: An Analysis of Current Benchmark Datasets and a Roadmap for Doing a Better Job, LREC 2016

seen.corpus: entity-linking benchmark datasets, compared for their annotation conventions
seen.document: the convention itself, which the datasets do not agree on
seen.observer: van Erp, Mendes, Paulheim, Ilievski, Plu, Rizzo, Waitelonis
seen.organisation: van Erp, Mendes, Paulheim, Ilievski, Plu, Rizzo, Waitelonis
seen.excerpt: Handling redundancy — annotating only the first vs. annotating all occurrences of an entity. — And, in the same list: Offset calculation — using 0 vs. using 1 as the initial identifier.

prevention.note: the convention can be declared and checked; what code cannot do is recover the count from a corpus annotated the other way

repair.note: not a fault of the graph: a property of the corpus, which is why it is CORPUS_PARAMETER

proposed_severity.reason: No fact disappears, so nothing looks wrong. What changes is the count of mentions, and any edge weighted by that count is divided by however many times the entity recurred. A graph whose weights come from mention counts is therefore built on a convention nobody wrote down, and two corpora annotated differently are not comparable. It is the exact shape of a silent decision that skews a weighted graph.
proposed_severity.reason_fr: Aucun fait ne disparaît, donc rien n'a l'air faux. Ce qui change, c'est le compte de mentions, et toute arête pondérée par ce compte est divisée par le nombre de fois où l'entité revenait. Un graphe dont les poids viennent de comptes de mentions repose alors sur une convention que personne n'a écrite, et deux corpus annotés différemment ne sont pas comparables. C'est la forme même de la décision silencieuse qui fausse un graphe pondéré.
proposed_severity.proposed_by: Claude Banc à vérité connue (LLM agent)
